blocks.title: Penetration Testing Approaches and Reconnaissance comparison
Penetration Testing Approaches and Reconnaissance exam shortcuts
items: Tester has diagrams, credentials, and source code → KNOWN ENVIRONMENT
This is white-box style testing.
Example: Tester receives full architecture details.
Tester gets some internal information → PARTIALLY KNOWN
This is gray-box style testing.
Example: Tester receives one user account and partial network details.
Tester starts with only public information → UNKNOWN ENVIRONMENT
This is black-box style testing.
Example: Tester knows only the company's domain name.
Research using public sources only → PASSIVE RECON
Passive recon avoids direct interaction with target systems.
Example: Review public DNS and social media.
Port scanning or enumeration → ACTIVE RECON
Active recon directly touches the target.
Example: Scan exposed services.
Attack and defense teams collaborate during testing → INTEGRATED
Integrated testing combines offensive and defensive perspectives.
Example: Red and blue teams work together as a purple team.
Attempt to bypass badge controls → PHYSICAL PEN TEST
The target is physical access rather than only digital systems.
Example: Tester attempts tailgating into a secured area.
blocks.example: For audit questions, focus on who performs the review. For penetration testing, focus on the tester's knowledge level and whether reconnaissance touches the target.

questions.q: A tester is given architecture diagrams, credentials, and source code before the assessment. What type of environment is this?
questions.explanation: A known environment gives the tester extensive prior knowledge, similar to white-box testing.

questions.q: A tester receives one user account and partial network information but not full architecture details. What type of environment is this?
questions.explanation: A partially known environment provides limited prior knowledge, similar to gray-box testing.

questions.q: A tester begins with only the organization's public domain name and no internal information. What type of environment is this?
questions.explanation: An unknown environment provides little or no prior knowledge, similar to black-box testing.

questions.q: A tester gathers employee names, public DNS records, and social-media information without interacting with target systems. Which reconnaissance type is this?
questions.explanation: Passive reconnaissance uses public or indirect sources without touching the target systems.

questions.q: A tester performs a port scan and service enumeration against target systems. Which reconnaissance type is this?
questions.explanation: Active reconnaissance directly interacts with the target.

questions.q: Red-team and blue-team members work together during an assessment to improve attack detection and response. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Integrated testing combines offensive and defensive perspectives, often called purple teaming.

questions.q: A tester attempts to tailgate into a secure facility and bypass badge controls. Which type of penetration testing is this?
questions.explanation: Physical penetration testing evaluates physical access controls.

questions.q: A penetration test focuses on emulating attacker behavior to exploit technical weaknesses. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Offensive penetration testing uses attacker techniques to identify and exploit weaknesses.

questions.q: A test is primarily designed to validate that monitoring, detection, and incident response controls work correctly. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Defensive penetration testing focuses on validating defensive controls and response capabilities.
